groups.title: Section A · 第 1 篇 · 1–4 题
groups.material:
W: Wow, I would give anything to be more like Audrey Hepburn.
M: I never really understood why so many girls were such big fans of her. I mean, I've seen the famous films, Roman Holiday, Breakfast at Tiffany's and a few others, but I still don't fully get it. Was she that great of an actress?
W: Well, for me, my adoration goes beyond her movies. She had such a classic elegance about her. She was always so poised, in part because she spent years training as a ballet dancer before becoming an actress.
M: Why didn't she stick to dancing as a career?
W: It seems it was fate. She suffered from inadequate nutrition during the war, and therefore, a career as a professional dancer would have been too demanding on her body. So she focused on acting instead. Roman Holiday was her first big break which made her a star.
M: Was that the film that opened with her shopping for jewelry in New York City? You know, in the scene, she was wearing a black dress and dark sunglasses with a pearl necklace and long black gloves. I see the photo of her in that costume everywhere.
W: No, that one is Breakfast At Tiffany's. That costume is often referred to as the most famous little black dress of all time. Her character in that film is very outgoing and charming, even though in real life, Audrey always described herself as shy and quiet.
M: So what did she do after her acting career?
W: She dedicated much of her life to helping children in need. Her family received international aid during the war when she was growing up. I think that left a big impression on her. That's where I got the idea to volunteer for children's charity next weekend.
M: I'll join you. I may not be as charming as Audrey Hepburn, but I'm all for supporting a good cause.

groups.title: Section A · 第 2 篇 · 5–8 题
groups.material:
W: So, how is our presentation about the restructuring of the company coming along?
M: Fine. I'm putting the finishing touches to it now.
M: …But we'll have to be prepared for questions.
W: Yes, there's already a feeling that this is a top down change. We really need to get everyone on board.
M: Well, there's been an extensive consultation period.
W: I know, but there's always the feeling that if it isn't broke, don't fix it.
M: People are worried about their jobs, too. I think we need to stress that while there will be some job changes, there won't be anyone getting dismissed. In fact, we're looking to take on more staff.
W: Agreed. You can hardly blame people for worrying though. We need to make it clear that it's not just change for change's sake. In other words, we really must make the case for why we are doing it.
W: …So what's the outline of the presentation?
M: I'll start with a brief review of the reasons for the change that we really need to make a clean break to restart growth. After that I'll outline the new company's structures and who's going where. Then I'll hand it over to you to discuss the timeline and summarize and we'll take questions together at the end. Anything else?
W: Oh, yeah, we should let the staff know the channels of communication, you know, who they can contact or direct questions to about these changes?
M: Yes, and we can collect some frequently asked questions and present some general answers.
W: Um, and we'll make the presentation and the questions available via the company's own computer network, right?
M: Yes, we'll make a page on the network where staff can download all the details.
W: All right. Perhaps we should do a practice round of the presentation first.
M: You bet.

groups.title: Section B · 第 1 篇 · 9–11 题
groups.material:
Airline passengers have to deal with a lot these days, getting bumped from flights and losing luggage on top of the general anxiety that nervous passengers always feel.
At the Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport, miniature horses deliver a calming force two times a month. Denver and Ruby are two of the 34 therapy horses brought in from a local farm. They can usually be found in the ticket counter area interacting with travelers.
More than 30 airports across the country now have therapy dogs. San Francisco has a therapy pig. San Jose, California, began a dog program after the terrorist attacks of September 11. Since its beginning, the program has now grown and has 21 therapy dogs and a therapy cat.
The animals don't get startled. They have had hundreds of hours of airport training, so they are used to having luggage and people crowding around them. These professional animals are probably better at finding their way in the airports than the most frequent of travelers.
The passengers often say that seeing animals makes them feel much better and helps them to calm down before a flight. This little bit of support can sometimes make a big difference. Some passengers enjoy the animals so much that they call the airport to schedule flights around their visits.
Visits to nursing homes and schools are also a regular part of the horses' schedule. Their owner is already working on a new idea for a therapy animal—donkeys.

groups.title: Section B · 第 2 篇 · 12–15 题
groups.material:
Hello, viewers. Today I'm standing at the 2000-year-old Roman-era site. Here the brightly-colored scenes that once decorated a mansion are being dug up. These scenes are turning up in the southern French city of Arles, surprising the historians who have been working here since 2014.
Patches of paint still cling to the stone walls of the bedroom and reception hall. Some of these painted walls are preserved in places to a height of one meter. In addition, thousands of fragments that fell off the walls have been recovered.
These pieces have been put back together with great care and display a variety of images. Some of these images include figures never seen before in France, such as a woman playing a stringed instrument, possibly a character from mythology.
The paintings were done with such skill and with such expensive dyes that experts believe the artists originally came from Italy. They were likely hired by one of the city's elite.
Perhaps a Roman official wanted Pompeii-like interior to remind him of home. He was probably stationed in this provincial trading port founded in 46 B.C. as a colony for veterans of the Roman army. Or maybe a wealthy local wanted to show off his worldly sophistication.
The paintings may yield even more stunning surprises as additional sections are put together, like pieces of a puzzle. Whoever it was that created such magnificent pieces of art, they surely had no idea that their work would still be around thousands of years later.

groups.title: Section C · 第 1 篇 · 16–18 题
groups.material:
Good afternoon, class. Today I want to discuss with you a new approach to empirical research.
In the past, scientists often worked alone. They were confined to the university or research center where they worked.
Today, though, we are seeing mergers of some of the greatest scientific minds, regardless of their location. There has never been a better time for collaborations with foreign scientists.
In fact, the European Union is taking the lead. Spurred on by funding policies, half of European research articles had international co-authors in 2007. This is more than twice the level of two decades ago. The European Union's level of international co-authorship is about twice that of the United States, Japan and India.
Even so, the levels in these countries are also rising. This is a sign of the continued allure of creating scientific coalitions across borders.
Andrew Schubert, a researcher at the Institute for Science Policy Research, says that the rising collaboration is partly out of necessity. This necessity comes with the rise of big science. Many scientific endeavors have become more complicated. These new complications require the money and labor of many nations.
But he says collaborations have also emerged because of increased possibilities. The Internet allows like-minded scientists to find each other. Simultaneously, dramatic drops in communication costs ease long-distance interactions.
And there is a reward. Studies of citation counts show that internationally co-authored papers have better visibility. Schubert says international collaboration is a way to spread ideas in wider and wider circles.
Caroline Wagner, a research scientist at George Washington University, notes that international collaborations offer additional flexibility. Whereas local collaborations sometimes persist past the point of usefulness because of social or academic obligations, international ones can be cultivated and dropped more freely.
The collaborative trend is true across scientific disciplines. Some fields, though, have a greater tendency for it.
Particle physicists and astronomers collaborate often. This is because they must share expensive facilities. Mathematicians, by contrast, tend historically towards solitude. As a consequence, they lag behind other disciplines. However, Wagner says partnerships are rising there, too.
The level of collaboration also varies from country to country. There are historical and political reasons as to why collaborations emerge, says Wagner. This rise is also apparently boosted by policies embedded in European framework funding schemes. These policies underlie funding requirements that often require teamwork.

groups.title: Section C · 第 2 篇 · 19–21 题
groups.material:
Good evening. In 1959, on the day that I was born, a headline in Life magazine proclaimed "Target Venus: There May be Life There!" It told of how scientists rode a balloon to an altitude of 80,000 feet to make telescope observations of Venus's atmosphere, and how their discovery of water raised hopes that there could be living things there.
As a kid, I thrilled to tales of adventure and Isaac Asimov's juvenile science-fiction novel Lucky Starr and the Oceans of Venus. For many of my peers, though, Venus quickly lost its romance.
The very first thing that scientists discovered with the mission to another planet was that Venus was not at all the Earthly paradise that fiction had portrayed. It is nearly identical to our own planet in bulk properties such as mass, density, and size. But its surface has been cooked and dried by an ocean of carbon dioxide.
Trapped in the burning death-grip of a runaway greenhouse effect, Venus has long been held up as a cautionary tale for everything that could go wrong on a planet like Earth. As a possible home for alien life, it has been voted the planet least likely to succeed.
But I have refused to give up on Venus, and over the years my stubborn loyalty has been justified. The rocky views glimpsed by Venera, and other Russian landers suggested a tortured volcanic history. That was confirmed in the early 1990s by the American Magellan orbiter, which used radar to peer through the planet's thick clouds and map out a rich, varied, and dynamic surface. The surface formed mostly in the last billion years, which makes it fresher and more recently active than any rocky planet other than Earth.
Russian and American spacecraft also found hints that its ancient climate might have been wetter, cooler, and possibly even friendly to life. Measurements of density and composition imply that Venus originally formed out of basically the same stuff as Earth. That presumably included much more water than the tiny trace we find blowing in the thick air today.
Thus, our picture of Venus at around the time life was getting started on Earth is one of warm oceans, probably rich with organic molecules, splashing around rocky shores and volcanic vents. The sun was considerably less bright back then. So, Venus was arguably a cozier habitat for life than Earth.

groups.title: Section C · 第 3 篇 · 22–25 题
groups.material:
I'm a psychology professor at the University of British Columbia. I specialize in Cultural Psychology, examining similarities and differences between East Asians and North Americans.
Our research team has been looking at cultural differences in self-enhancing motivations, how people have positive feelings towards not only themselves, but things connected to themselves. For example, when you own something, you view it as more valuable than when you don't own it. It's called the "endowment effect". The strength of that effect is stronger in Western cultures than in Eastern cultures. So we've been looking at other ways of seeing whether this motivation to view oneself positively is shaped by cultural experiences.
We've also started to look at how culture shapes sleep. We are still in the exploratory stages of this project, although what's noteworthy is that East Asians on average sleep about an hour and a half less each night than North Americans do. And it's not a more efficient sleep, not like they're compressing relatively more value out of their hours. Other studies have found that even infants in East Asia sleep about an hour less than European infants. So we're trying to figure out how culture shapes the way you sleep.
Our experiment does not take place in a sleep lab. Instead, we lend people motion-detecting watches, and they wear them for a week at a time. Whenever they are not having a shower or swimming, they keep it on. These kinds of watches are used in sleep studies as a way of measuring how long people are sleeping, how efficient their sleep is, and whether they are waking up in the night.
Ideally, I'd like to take this into a controlled lab environment. We'll see where the research points us. We usually start off with the more affordable methods and if everything looks promising, then it will justify trying to build a sleep lab and study sleep across cultures that way.
Why do we study sleep? Sleep is something that has really been an unexplored topic cross-culturally. I'm attracted to it because culture isn't something that only shapes the way our minds operate; it shapes the way our bodies operate too, and sleep is at the intersection of those.

questions.prompt: What does the man say he never really understood?
options: Why Roman Holiday was more famous than Breakfast at Tiffany's.
Why Audrey Hepburn had more female fans than male ones.
Why the woman wanted to be like Audrey Hepburn.
Why so many girls adored Audrey Hepburn.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the man say he never really understood? 

 【翻译】 男士说他从未真正理解什么？ 
 A)  为什么《罗马假日》比《蒂凡尼的早餐》更有名。 
 B)  为什么Audrey Hepburn的女性影迷多于男性影迷。 
 C)  为什么这位女士想要成为像Audrey Hepburn那样的人。 
 D)  为什么那么多女孩崇拜Audrey Hepburn。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Why so many girls adored Audrey Hepburn. 
 【定位】 P2 I never really understood why so many girls were such big fans of her. 
 我一直没真正弄明白，为什么那么多女孩是她的铁杆粉丝。 

 【信号】 说话人直陈"没弄懂" 。男方原话 I never really understood why so many girls were such big fans of her. 直接说出"never really understood"，这正是题干要找的"他不理解的内容"——说话人主动表态的句子就是答案句，不必再绕。 

 【替换】 so many girls were such big fans of her ↔ so many girls adored Audrey Hepburn be big fans of = adored 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A 把录音里出现过的 Roman Holiday 与 Breakfast at Tiffany's 两个片名拼成"哪部更出名"，可男方说的是没懂"女孩为何爱她"，根本没比较两片名气，属听到片名就想选的原词陷阱。  借用原文：I've seen the famous films, Roman Holiday, Breakfast at Tiffany's 

 B) 偷换概念 B 说"为何女粉多于男粉"，但录音只说 so many girls were such big fans，从未把女粉和男粉作数量比较；它偷偷把"很多女孩喜欢"扭成"女比男多"，属偷换概念。  借用原文：so many girls were such big fans of her 

 C) 张冠李戴 C 说"女方为何想像 Audrey"，可没懂的是男方，女方第1段说的是 I would give anything to be more like Audrey Hepburn（她自己的向往）。把"女方的愿望"安到"男方不解的内容"上，属张冠李戴。  借用原文：I would give anything to be more like Audrey Hepburn

questions.prompt: What prevented Audrey Hepburn from becoming a professional dancer?
options: Her unique personality.
Her physical condition.
Her shift of interest to performing arts.
Her family's suspension of financial aid.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What prevented Audrey Hepburn from becoming a professional dancer? 

 【翻译】 是什么阻止了Audrey Hepburn成为一名职业舞蹈演员？ 
 A)  她独特的个性。 
 B)  她的身体状况。 
 C)  她的兴趣转向了表演艺术。 
 D)  她的家庭中断了经济资助。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Her physical condition. 
 【定位】 P5 She suffered from inadequate nutrition during the war, and therefore, a career as a professional dancer would have been too demanding on her body. 
 战时她营养不良，因此，职业舞者这一行对她的身体来说会太过吃力。 

 【信号】 因果词 therefore 引出落点 。答案句以 and therefore 这个因果信号连接：前因是营养不良，后果是身体吃不消舞者职业。"therefore"后面正是题干要的"妨碍原因"，是听原因题最该锁定的信号词。 

 【替换】 too demanding on her body ↔ Her physical condition. 身体吃不消=身体状况 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 A"独特个性"在这段原因里完全没出现，录音讲的是营养与身体，不是性格阻碍了她跳舞，属原文未提及的捏造原因。 
 C) 答非所问 C 说"兴趣转向表演艺术"，录音确有 So she focused on acting instead，但那是"身体原因→所以改行演戏"的结果，不是阻止她跳舞的原因；考生易凭"她后来去演戏"的常识顺手选它，属答非所问。  借用原文：So she focused on acting instead. 

 D) 未提及 D"家里中断了经济资助"录音从未提及，妨碍她的是身体不是缺钱；它借"家庭/经济"这类听起来合理的常见理由凑数，属未提及。
questions.spoken_text: What prevented Audrey Hepburn from becoming a professional dancer?

questions.prompt: What do we learn about Audrey Hepburn in real life?
options: She was not an outgoing person.
She was modest and hardworking.
She was easy-going on the whole.
She was usually not very optimistic.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about Audrey Hepburn in real life? 

 【翻译】 关于现实生活中的Audrey Hepburn我们了解到什么？ 
 A)  她不是一个外向的人。 
 B)  她谦逊且勤奋。 
 C)  她总体上随和。 
 D)  她通常不太乐观。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） She was not an outgoing person. 
 【定位】 P7 Her character in that film is very outgoing and charming, even though in real life, Audrey always described herself as shy and quiet. 
 她在那部电影里的角色非常外向、迷人，尽管现实中 Audrey 总把自己形容为腼腆而文静。 

 【信号】 让步词 even though 后才是真意 。答案句用 even though in real life 这一让步信号把"银幕形象"与"真实本人"分开：even though 后面的 shy and quiet 才是题干 in real life 要的答案。让步/转折后才是落点，前半的 outgoing 是干扰。 

 【替换】 shy and quiet ↔ She was not an outgoing person. shy=not outgoing 

 【排除】 B) 未提及 B"谦虚勤奋"中"hardworking"录音从未提及；虽然 shy 与"谦虚"略有交集易混，但"勤奋"完全没依据，属未提及。 
 C) 原词陷阱 C"总体随和"对应的是录音里 very outgoing and charming——可那是"电影角色"(her character in that film)的样子，不是真实的她；考生听到 outgoing 就想选，正中原词陷阱。  借用原文：Her character in that film is very outgoing and charming 

 D) 未提及 D"通常不太乐观"录音里毫无对应，她被描述为 shy and quiet，与"乐观与否"无关；它利用与 A 同样的 not 句式制造混淆，属未提及。
questions.spoken_text: What do we learn about Audrey Hepburn in real life?

questions.prompt: Why did Audrey Hepburn devote much of her life to charity after her acting career?
options: She was influenced by the roles she played in the films.
Her parents taught her to sympathize with the needy.
She learned to volunteer when she was a child.
Her family benefited from other people's help.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why did Audrey Hepburn devote much of her life to charity after her acting career? 

 【翻译】 为什么Audrey Hepburn在演艺生涯结束后将大部分生命投入到慈善事业？ 
 A)  她受到自己在电影中扮演的角色的影响。 
 B)  她的父母教导她同情有需要的人。 
 C)  她小时候就学会了做志愿者。 
 D)  她的家庭受益于他人的帮助。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Her family benefited from other people's help. 
 【定位】 P9 Her family received international aid during the war when she was growing up. I think that left a big impression on her. 
 她成长期间，她的家庭在战时受到了国际援助。我想那给她留下了深刻印象。 

 【信号】 回忆受助 + left a big impression 点出触发 。答案句先陈述往事 Her family received international aid during the war，再用 that left a big impression on her 点明"正是这件事触动了她"——这种"往事+留下深刻印象"的溯源句，就是动机题的答案信号。 

 【替换】 Her family received international aid during the war ↔ Her family benefited from other people's help. received aid=benefited from help 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 A"受所演角色影响"录音从未提及她的善心来自电影角色；动机原文明确归到"家庭受助"，属未提及。 
 B) 偷换概念 B说"父母教她同情弱者"，录音只说家庭"受过援助"，并未说父母"教导"她；它把"family"原词留着却换了动机机制，属偷换概念。  借用原文：Her family received international aid during the war 

 C) 原词陷阱 C"小时候学会做志愿"借用了录音 when she was growing up（成长期间）这个童年时间，但原文说的是"小时候家里受助"，不是"小时候学会志愿"；听到"小时候"就想选，正中原词陷阱。  借用原文：when she was growing up
questions.spoken_text: Why did Audrey Hepburn devote much of her life to charity after her acting career?

questions.prompt: What is the man going to do?
options: Give a presentation.
Raise some questions.
Start a new company.
Attend a board meeting.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is the man going to do? 

 【翻译】 这位男士将要做什么? 
 A)  做一个陈述。 
 B)  提出一些问题。 
 C)  创办一家新公司。 
 D)  参加董事会会议。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Give a presentation. 
 【定位】 P2 M: Fine. I'm putting the finishing touches to it now. 
 男：挺好的，我正在给它做最后的收尾。 

 【信号】 被问者的直接应答 。女士问 how is our presentation about the restructuring of the company coming along，男士紧接着应答 I'm putting the finishing touches to it now——一问一答里被问者亲口说在弄这份汇报，应答处即答案句。 

 【替换】 I'm putting the finishing touches to it now ↔ Give a presentation. 代词it回指presentation 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 录音里 we'll have to be prepared for questions 提到 questions，但那是说要准备应对听众提问，不是男士自己去提问；Raise some questions. 把这个词搬来错安在男士头上。  借用原文：we'll have to be prepared for questions 

 C) 原词陷阱 录音反复出现 company、new structures 等词，Start a new company. 借这些词拼出开新公司，但全篇只在谈重组现有公司，从没说要创办新公司。  借用原文：I'll outline the new company's structures 

 D) 未提及 Attend a board meeting. 听着像公司重组场合该有的事，但录音通篇只说 presentation，从未提 board meeting，属凭场景常识臆造、未提及。
questions.spoken_text: What is the man going to do?

questions.prompt: What does the man say about the restructuring?
options: It will cut production costs.
It will raise productivity.
No staff will be dismissed.
No new staff will be hired.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the man say about the restructuring? 

 【翻译】 关于重组,这位男士说了什么? 
 A)  它将降低生产成本。 
 B)  它将提高生产率。 
 C)  不会有员工被解雇。 
 D)  不会招聘新员工。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） No staff will be dismissed. 
 【定位】 P7 M: People are worried about their jobs, too. I think we need to stress that while there will be some job changes, there won't be anyone getting dismissed. In fact, we're looking to take on more staff. 
 男：大家也在担心自己的饭碗。我觉得我们得强调，虽然会有一些岗位调整，但不会有任何人被裁掉。事实上，我们还打算多招些人。 

 【信号】 强调句won't加转折 。男士用 stress 引出重点，再借 while there will be…but there won't be anyone getting dismissed 的让步转折，把真意压在 won't 之后——不裁人才是他要传达的核心。 

 【替换】 there won't be anyone getting dismissed ↔ No staff will be dismissed. won't anyone等于No staff 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 It will cut production costs. 像是重组该有的好处，但录音从没提 production costs 或降成本，是凭常识臆造的未提及项。 
 B) 未提及 It will raise productivity. 同样是想当然的重组好处，录音里 productivity 一词从未出现，属未提及。 
 D) 与原文相反 录音末句 we're looking to take on more staff 明说要多招人，No new staff will be hired. 借走 staff 却把意思反成不招新人，极性正好相反。  借用原文：we're looking to take on more staff
questions.spoken_text: What does the man say about the restructuring?

questions.prompt: What will the man explain first?
options: The timeline of restructuring.
The reasons for restructuring.
The communication channels.
The company's new missions.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What will the man explain first? 

 【翻译】 这位男士将首先解释什么? 
 A)  重组的时间表。 
 B)  重组的原因。 
 C)  沟通渠道。 
 D)  公司的新使命。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） The reasons for restructuring. 
 【定位】 P10 M: I'll start with a brief review of the reasons for the change that we really need to make a clean break to restart growth. After that I'll outline the new company's structures and who's going where. 
 男：我会先简要回顾一下这次变革的原因，也就是我们确实需要彻底切割、重启增长。之后我会讲新公司的架构以及谁去哪里。 

 【信号】 次序词start with 。男士用 I'll start with a brief review of the reasons for the change 的 start with 标出第一项，再用 After that 引出第二项，次序词清楚划定先讲原因。 

 【替换】 start with a brief review of the reasons for the change ↔ The reasons for restructuring. reasons for the change即重组原因 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 The timeline of restructuring. 里的 timeline 录音确实提到，但那是 hand it over to you to discuss the timeline——时间线交给女士讲、且在后面，不是男士先讲的。  借用原文：hand it over to you to discuss the timeline 

 C) 原词陷阱 channels 在 we should let the staff know the channels of communication 出现过，但那是后面才聊到的内容、且非男士开篇先讲，The communication channels. 张冠李戴又错位。  借用原文：the channels of communication 

 D) 偷换概念 录音说男士第二项讲 the new company's structures，The company's new missions. 把 structures 偷换成 missions，且 missions 全篇未提，既错序又改义。  借用原文：I'll outline the new company's structures

 女：嗯，而且我们会把汇报和问答放到公司自己的电脑网络上，对吧？男：对，我们会在网络上做一个页面，员工可以在上面下载所有细节。

 make a page on the network where staff can download all the details ↔ By visiting the company's own computer network. 上网下载即访问网络

questions.prompt: What is special about the Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky international airport?
options: It helps passengers to take care of their pet animals.
It has animals to help passengers carry their language.
It uses therapy animals to soothe nervous passengers.
It allows passengers to have animals travels with them.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is special about the Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky international airport? 

 【翻译】 辛辛那提/北肯塔基国际机场有什么特别之处? 
 A)  它帮助乘客照顾他们的宠物。 
 B)  它有动物帮助乘客搬运行李。 
 C)  它使用治疗动物来安抚紧张的乘客。 
 D)  它允许乘客携带动物一起旅行。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） It uses therapy animals to soothe nervous passengers. 
 【定位】 P2 At the Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport, miniature horses deliver a calming force two times a month. 
 在辛辛那提/北肯塔基国际机场，小型马每月两次带来一股令人平静的力量。 

 【信号】 专有名词复现处即答案句定位锚 。录音里 At the Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport 原样念出了题干中的机场名，这个专有名词的复现就是定位信号——紧跟其后的 miniature horses deliver a calming force 点明这家机场的特别之处是用小马带来"平静的力量"。 

 【替换】 deliver a calming force ↔ soothe nervous passengers calming force = soothe，同义改写 
 the general anxiety that nervous passengers always feel ↔ nervous passengers nervous passengers 原词点明被安抚对象 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 take care of their pet animals 借用了录音反复出现的 animals、passengers，制造"听到就想选"的诱惑，但录音说的是机场"提供"动物来安抚旅客，从未提到帮旅客照看"他们自己的宠物"，方向反了。  借用原文：interacting with travelers 

 B) 原词陷阱 carry their language 听感上蹭了录音里 luggage（行李）这个词（选项 language 本身亦显错位），但录音提 luggage 是说动物习惯了 having luggage and people crowding around them"行李和人群围着自己"，并非动物帮旅客搬运，属盗用原词的答非所问。  借用原文：having luggage and people crowding around them 

 D) 偷换概念 allows passengers to have animals travels with them 用 animals、travel 拼出"允许旅客带动物同行"，迎合常识，但录音讲的是机场"安排"治疗动物去安抚旅客，主语和方向都不是"旅客带自己的动物"，张冠李戴。  借用原文：therapy horses brought in from a local farm

questions.prompt: What are the trained animals probably capable of doing in an airport?
options: Avoiding possible dangers.
Finding their way around.
Identifying drug smugglers.
Looking after sick passengers.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What are the trained animals probably capable of doing in an airport? 

 【翻译】 受过训练的动物在机场可能具备什么能力? 
 A)  避免可能的危险。 
 B)  找到周围的路。 
 C)  识别毒品走私者。 
 D)  照顾生病的乘客。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Finding their way around. 
 【定位】 P4 These professional animals are probably better at finding their way in the airports than the most frequent of travelers. 
 这些专业动物在机场里认路的本事，大概比最常飞的旅客还要强。 

 【信号】 比较级 better at + 题干 probably 双重信号 。答案句用比较级 better at finding their way in the airports than the most frequent of travelers 强调动物某项本领胜过常客，且题干的 probably 正对应原文的 probably，这种"突出某能力"的比较句就是描述动物能力的答案句信号。 

 【替换】 finding their way in the airports ↔ Finding their way around finding their way 近乎原词的同义对应 

 【排除】 A) 过度推断 Avoiding possible dangers 蹭了录音 The animals don't get startled"动物不受惊"的语境，听感像"避开危险"，但"不受惊"说的是性情稳、不被环境吓到，并非"会避险"，属过度引申。  借用原文：The animals don't get startled 

 C) 未提及 Identifying drug smugglers 利用大家对"机场犬"的常识印象（缉毒），极具迷惑性，但全篇讲的是治疗动物安抚旅客，从未提到识别毒品或走私者，属凭常识无中生有。 
 D) 偷换概念 Looking after sick passengers 借了录音高频词 passengers，但动物的作用是安抚紧张旅客、让人平静，录音没说照看"生病的"旅客，sick 属于凭空添加的限定，张冠李戴。  借用原文：helps them to calm down before a flight
questions.spoken_text: What are the trained animals probably capable of doing in an airport?

questions.prompt: What do some passengers try to do?
options: Schedule their flights around the animal visits.
Photograph the therapy animals at the airport.
Keep some animals for therapeutic purposes.
Bring their animals on board their plane.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do some passengers try to do? 

 【翻译】 一些乘客试图做什么? 
 A)  围绕动物探访安排他们的航班。 
 B)  在机场拍摄治疗动物。 
 C)  为治疗目的饲养一些动物。 
 D)  把他们的动物带上飞机。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Schedule their flights around the animal visits. 
 【定位】 P5 Some passengers enjoy the animals so much that they call the airport to schedule flights around their visits. 
 有些旅客太喜欢这些动物了，以至于打电话给机场，把航班安排在动物来访的时间前后。 

 【信号】 Some passengers 主语复现 + so…that 结果句 。答案句以 Some passengers 复现题干主语开头，又用 so much that 引出结果 they call the airport to schedule flights around their visits，主语对齐加结果句双重信号锁定这就是描述"某些旅客所做之事"的答案句。 

 【替换】 schedule flights around their visits ↔ Schedule their flights around the animal visits schedule flights around…visits 近原词对应 

 【排除】 B) 未提及 Photograph the therapy animals at the airport 利用"旅客喜欢动物"自然联想到拍照的常识，但录音说旅客喜欢动物的表现是"打电话安排航班"，从头到尾没提拍照，属无中生有。 
 C) 原词陷阱 Keep some animals for therapeutic purposes 蹭了全篇的 therapy / therapeutic 与 animals，但治疗动物是机场从农场引进的，录音从没说旅客"自己留养动物作治疗用"，盗用原词后答非所问。  借用原文：therapy horses brought in from a local farm 

 D) 偷换概念 Bring their animals on board their plane 借 animals 一词编出"旅客带动物登机"，但录音里旅客是被动物安抚、围着动物来访安排航班，并非把自己的动物带上飞机，方向相反。  借用原文：seeing animals makes them feel much better

questions.prompt: Where is the speaker standing?
options: Beside a beautifully painted wall in Arles.
Beside the gate of an ancient Roman city.
At the site of an ancient Roman mansion.
At the entrance to a reception hall in Rome.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Where is the speaker standing? 

 【翻译】 说话者站在哪里? 
 A)  在阿尔勒一面绘有精美图画的墙壁旁边。 
 B)  在一座古罗马城市的大门旁边。 
 C)  在一座古罗马宅邸的遗址处。 
 D)  在罗马一个接待大厅的入口处。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） At the site of an ancient Roman mansion. 
 【定位】 P1 Today I'm standing at the 2000-year-old Roman-era site. Here the brightly-colored scenes that once decorated a mansion are being dug up. 
 今天我正站在这处有两千年历史的罗马时代遗址上。这里,曾经装饰一座宅邸的鲜艳壁画正被发掘出来。 

 【信号】 现场指示语standing at 。答案句的信号是说话人自报方位的现场指示语 I'm standing at the 2000-year-old Roman-era site,紧接 scenes that once decorated a mansion 点明这处遗址正是一座宅邸所在,正是 where 的落点。 

 【替换】 Roman-era site ↔ the site of an ancient Roman mansion Roman-era等于ancient Roman 
 scenes that once decorated a mansion ↔ mansion 宅邸点题 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 原文后文确实提到这些发现出现在 Arles,本项 Beside a beautifully painted wall in Arles. 借走 Arles 这个地名,但说话人自报的是站在遗址上(standing at the site),并非紧挨某面 wall,把出现地点偷换成贴墙站立,属原词陷阱。  借用原文：These scenes are turning up in the southern French city of Arles 

 B) 偷换概念 本项 Beside the gate of an ancient Roman city. 沿用了 ancient Roman 这一真实表述,却把说话人所站的 site(遗址)偷换成 gate of a city(城市的城门),原文从未提及任何城门,属盗用原词后偷换概念。  借用原文：the 2000-year-old Roman-era site 

 D) 张冠李戴 本项 At the entrance to a reception hall in Rome. 把后文第二段才出现的 reception hall(接待厅)挪到此处,又把地点说成 in Rome;但说话人站的是法国南部 Arles 的遗址、且非站在接待厅入口,属张冠李戴式的原词拼贴。  借用原文：Patches of paint still cling to the stone walls of the bedroom and reception hall

questions.prompt: What do the thousands of fragments display when they are put back together?
options: A number of different images.
A number of mythological heroes.
Various musical instruments.
Paintings by famous French artists.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do the thousands of fragments display when they are put back together? 

 【翻译】 成千上万的碎片重新拼合在一起时展现出什么? 
 A)  许多不同的图像。 
 B)  许多神话英雄。 
 C)  各种乐器。 
 D)  法国著名艺术家的画作。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） A number of different images. 
 【定位】 P3 These pieces have been put back together with great care and display a variety of images. 
 这些碎片被非常细心地重新拼合起来,呈现出多种多样的图像。 

 【信号】 原词display直接对接 。答案句信号是题干 put back together 与 display 在原文 put back together with great care and display a variety of images 几乎原样复现,顺着这一动作即锁定其宾语 a variety of images。 

 【替换】 a variety of images ↔ A number of different images a variety of等于different 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 原文确实提到 a woman playing a stringed instrument 可能是 a character from mythology,本项 A number of mythological heroes. 借走 mythology 一词,却把一个举例放大成全部内容,且原文是 character(角色) 而非 heroes(英雄),属原词陷阱兼以偏概全。  借用原文：possibly a character from mythology 

 C) 原词陷阱 原文举例提到一名女子 playing a stringed instrument,本项 Various musical instruments. 借走 instrument,却把单个举例夸成 various musical instruments,展示的是图像而非各种乐器,属原词陷阱。  借用原文：a woman playing a stringed instrument 

 D) 答非所问 本项 Paintings by famous French artists. 把绘画的来源说成法国名家,但原文第四段恰恰说工匠很可能来自意大利(came from Italy),且本题问展示的内容而非作者,属张冠李戴与答非所问。  借用原文：experts believe the artists originally came from Italy

questions.prompt: What makes experts think the paintings were done by artists from Italy?
options: The originality and expertise shown.
The worldly sophistication displayed.
The stunning images vividly depicted.
The impressive skills and costly dyes.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What makes experts think the paintings were done by artists from Italy? 

 【翻译】 是什么让专家认为这些画作是由来自意大利的艺术家完成的? 
 A)  所展现的独创性和专业技艺。 
 B)  所展现的世俗老练。 
 C)  所描绘的令人惊叹的生动图像。 
 D)  令人印象深刻的技艺和昂贵的染料。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） The impressive skills and costly dyes. 
 【定位】 P4 The paintings were done with such skill and with such expensive dyes that experts believe the artists originally came from Italy. 
 这些壁画绘制得技艺如此高超、用料染料如此昂贵,以致专家相信这些艺术家原本来自意大利。 

 【信号】 such…that因果结构 。答案句信号是 done with such skill and with such expensive dyes that experts believe… 里的 such…that 因果结构:that 前面的 such skill 与 such expensive dyes 正是促成专家判断的两条依据。 

 【替换】 such skill ↔ The impressive skills such skill等于impressive skills 
 such expensive dyes ↔ costly dyes expensive等于costly 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 本项 The originality and expertise shown. 中 expertise(专业技艺) 看似贴近原文的 skill,但原文给的两条依据是 skill 与 expensive dyes,并未提 originality(原创性),本项漏掉染料、又添了原文没有的原创性,要素配不齐。  借用原文：done with such skill and with such expensive dyes 

 B) 原词陷阱 worldly sophistication 确在原文出现,但那是第五段说本地富人想借壁画炫耀见识,与专家判断画家来自意大利毫无关系,本项 The worldly sophistication displayed. 把别处原词搬来答非所问,属原词陷阱。  借用原文：a wealthy local wanted to show off his worldly sophistication 

 C) 原词陷阱 stunning 一词原文出现在末段说后续拼合或带来更惊人的发现,本项 The stunning images vividly depicted. 借走 stunning 描述图像生动,却与专家判断产地的依据无关,属原词陷阱。  借用原文：The paintings may yield even more stunning surprises

questions.prompt: What do we learn from the passage about the owner of the mansion?
options: His artistic taste is superb.
His identity remains unclear.
He was a collector of antiques.

questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn from the passage about the owner of the mansion? 

 【翻译】 从文章中我们了解到关于这座宅邸主人的什么信息? 
 A)  他的艺术品味极佳。 
 B)  他的身份仍不清楚。

 也许是某位罗马官员想要一处庞贝风格的室内装饰来勾起他的思乡之情……又或许是某位富有的本地人想要炫耀自己见多识广。 

 【信号】 perhaps与or maybe的猜测并列 。答案句信号是 Perhaps a Roman official 与 Or maybe a wealthy local 这组 perhaps…or maybe 的猜测并列:原文给出两种互斥的可能、用 or 连接却都不下定论,正说明主人身份未定。

 C) 未提及 原文通篇在讲出土的古罗马壁画,但从未说主人是古董收藏家,本项 He was a collector of antiques. 是借古迹话题臆造的身份,原文无对应。 
 D) 张冠李戴 原文说艺术家可能来自意大利(came from Italy)、又提这是一处贸易港,本项 He was a rich Italian merchant. 把 Italian 和 trading 拼成主人是富有的意大利商人,但 Italy 是说艺术家来源、且原文对主人是 official 还是 local 都未定,属张冠李戴。  借用原文：experts believe the artists originally came from Italy

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the research funding policies in the European Union?
options: They encourage international cooperation.
They lay stress on basic scientific research.
They place great emphasis on empirical studies.
They favour scientists from its member countries.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about the research funding policies in the European Union? 

 【翻译】 关于欧盟的科研资助政策，我们了解到什么？ 
 A)  它们鼓励国际合作。 
 B)  它们强调基础科学研究。 
 C)  它们非常重视实证研究。 
 D)  它们偏向来自其成员国的科学家。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） They encourage international cooperation. 
 【定位】 P4 In fact, the European Union is taking the lead. Spurred on by funding policies, half of European research articles had international co-authors in 2007. 
 事实上，欧盟正走在前列。在资助政策的推动下，2007 年有一半的欧洲研究论文拥有国际合著者。 

 【信号】 因果短语点出政策作用 。答案信号是因果短语 Spurred on by funding policies，它点明正是资助政策推动了国际合著的激增，这句把政策与国际合作直接挂钩，是承载答案的句子。 

 【替换】 Spurred on by funding policies, half of European research articles had international co-authors ↔ They encourage international cooperation. 推动合著等于鼓励合作 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 B 借了开篇 empirical research 与全篇科研话题制造熟悉感，但录音从未说政策侧重基础科研（basic research），讲的是推动国际合著，B 答非所问。  借用原文：a new approach to empirical research 

 C) 原词陷阱 C 盗用录音原词 empirical（实证），把它包装成政策侧重实证研究；但 empirical 只出现在开场点题，与资助政策的取向无关，属听到原词就想选的陷阱。  借用原文：empirical research 

 D) 与原文相反 D 利用 European Union 让人联想到成员国，称政策偏袒本国成员的科学家；但录音说政策推动的是跨国合著，方向恰恰是对外合作，D 把范围从对外合作偷改成对内偏袒，与原文相反。  借用原文：half of European research articles had international co-authors
questions.spoken_text: What do we learn about the research funding policies in the European Union?

questions.prompt: Why do researchers today favor international collaboration?
options: Many of them wish to win international recognition.
They believe that more hands will make light work.
They want to follow closely the international trend.
Many of their projects have become complicated.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why do researchers today favor international collaboration? 

 【翻译】 为什么当今的研究人员青睐国际合作？ 
 A)  他们中的许多人希望赢得国际认可。 
 B)  他们相信人多好办事。 
 C)  他们想要紧跟国际趋势。 
 D)  他们的许多项目已经变得复杂。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Many of their projects have become complicated. 
 【定位】 P6 the rising collaboration is partly out of necessity. This necessity comes with the rise of big science. Many scientific endeavors have become more complicated. These new complications require the money and labor of many nations. 
 合作的兴起部分出于必要。这种必要伴随大科学的兴起而来。许多科研项目已变得更为复杂。这些新的复杂性需要众多国家的资金和人力。 

 【信号】 out of necessity领出原因 。答案信号是表原因的短语 out of necessity，它领出合作兴起的缘由，随后用 Many scientific endeavors have become more complicated 把这个必要性落到实处，是承载答案的句群。 

 【替换】 Many scientific endeavors have become more complicated ↔ Many of their projects have become complicated. 项目即科研活动近义替换 

 【排除】 A) 答非所问 A 借了第八段 better visibility 谈论的国际认可这一好处，说成研究者想赢得国际认可的动机；但那是合作带来的回报，不是本题问的偏好原因，属答非所问。  借用原文：internationally co-authored papers have better visibility 

 B) 未提及 B 用谚语 more hands will make light work 表示人多力量大，听着像在说合作好处；但录音从未表达研究者因相信人多省力而合作，纯属未提及。 
 C) 原词陷阱 C 拼接全篇高频的 international 与趋势话题，说研究者想紧跟国际潮流；但录音讲合作上升是出于必要与可能性增多，从未提跟风国际潮流这一动机，属原词陷阱。  借用原文：creating scientific coalitions across borders
questions.spoken_text: Why do researchers today favor international collaboration?

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the field of mathematics?
options: It requires mathematicians to work independently.
It is faced with many unprecedented challenges.
It lags behind other disciplines in collaboration.
It calls for more research funding to catch up.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about the field of mathematics? 

 【翻译】 关于数学领域，我们了解到什么？ 
 A)  它要求数学家独立工作。 
 B)  它面临许多前所未有的挑战。 
 C)  它在合作方面落后于其他学科。 
 D)  它需要更多科研资金才能赶上。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） It lags behind other disciplines in collaboration. 
 【定位】 P11 Mathematicians, by contrast, tend historically towards solitude. As a consequence, they lag behind other disciplines. 
 相比之下，数学家历来倾向于独自工作。其结果是，他们在合作上落后于其他学科。 

 【信号】 对比加结果双信号 。答案信号是对比词 by contrast 加结果词 As a consequence：先以 by contrast 把数学家与爱合作的物理学家对照开，再用 As a consequence 引出落后这一结论，结论句即答案句。 

 【替换】 they lag behind other disciplines ↔ It lags behind other disciplines in collaboration. 落后表述近乎原句 

 【排除】 A) 偷换概念 A 借了 tend historically towards solitude 表达的独自工作，但录音说的是数学家历来倾向独处，而 A 说成数学要求数学家独立工作，把客观倾向偷换成强制要求，偷换概念。  借用原文：Mathematicians, by contrast, tend historically towards solitude. 

 B) 未提及 B 说数学面临诸多空前挑战，听着与全篇科研主题相合，但录音谈数学只说它因独处而落后，从未说它面临空前挑战，属未提及。 
 D) 原词陷阱 D 盗用全篇高频的 funding，又借结尾 partnerships are rising there, too 暗示的追赶，拼成数学呼吁更多资助以迎头赶上；但录音从没说数学要更多经费，属原词陷阱。  借用原文：funding requirements that often require teamwork
questions.spoken_text: What do we learn about the field of mathematics?

questions.prompt: What do we learn from the Life magazine article?
options: Scientists tried to send a balloon to Venus.
Scientists discovered water on Venus.
Scientists found Venus had atmosphere.
Scientists observed Venus from a space vehicle.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn from the Life magazine article? 

 【翻译】 我们从《生活》杂志的文章中了解到什么? 
 A)  科学家试图向金星发射气球。 
 B)  科学家在金星上发现了水。 
 C)  科学家发现金星有大气层。 
 D)  科学家从太空飞行器上观测金星。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Scientists discovered water on Venus. 
 【定位】 P1 It told of how scientists rode a balloon to an altitude of 80,000 feet to make telescope observations of Venus's atmosphere, and how their discovery of water raised hopes that there could be living things there. 
 文章讲述了科学家如何乘气球升到八万英尺高空、用望远镜观测金星的大气，以及他们发现水这件事如何让人们燃起 "那里可能有生命" 的希望。 

 【信号】 their discovery of water 是文章交代的核心成果 。整句铺陈了气球、高度、望远镜、大气一连串细节，但真正落点是 their discovery of water raised hopes that there could be living things there——"发现水" 才是这篇文章给出的关键结论，前面的气球和大气都是过程铺垫。 

 【替换】 their discovery of water ↔ discovered water on Venus 名词化 discovery 还原为动词 discovered 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 原文确实说科学家 rode a balloon（乘气球），但乘气球只是观测的手段；Scientists tried to send a balloon to Venus. 把 "乘气球升到高空观测" 偷换成 "试图把气球送往金星"，气球根本没飞向金星，是听到 balloon 就抢选的陷阱。  借用原文：scientists rode a balloon to an altitude of 80,000 feet 

 C) 原词陷阱 原文 make telescope observations of Venus's atmosphere 里 atmosphere 只是被观测的对象，文章并没说 "发现金星有大气"；Scientists found Venus had atmosphere. 把 "观测大气" 偷换成 "发现存在大气"，是借 atmosphere 这个原词答非所问。  借用原文：make telescope observations of Venus's atmosphere 

 D) 偷换概念 文章说的是 rode a balloon to an altitude of 80,000 feet to make telescope observations——在地球大气层内乘气球用望远镜远观，而非 observed Venus from a space vehicle（从太空飞行器上观测）。气球八万英尺远不等于进入太空，属于把手段升级、与原文不符。  借用原文：rode a balloon to an altitude of 80,000 feet to make telescope observations
questions.spoken_text: What do we learn from the Life magazine article?

questions.prompt: What are scientists' findings about Venus?
options: It resembles Earth in many aspects.
It is the same as fiction has portrayed.
It is a paradise of romance for alien life.
It undergoes geological changes like Earth.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What are scientists' findings about Venus? 

 【翻译】 科学家关于金星有哪些发现? 
 A)  它在许多方面与地球相似。 
 B)  它与科幻小说所描绘的一样。 
 C)  它是外星生命的浪漫天堂。 
 D)  它像地球一样经历地质变化。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） It resembles Earth in many aspects. 
 【定位】 P3 The very first thing that scientists discovered with the mission to another planet was that Venus was not at all the Earthly paradise that fiction had portrayed. It is nearly identical to our own planet in bulk properties such as mass, density, and size. 
 科学家在探测另一颗行星的任务中发现的头一件事，就是金星根本不是小说所描绘的那个 "地球般的天堂"。它在质量、密度、大小等总体性质上几乎与我们的地球如出一辙。 

 【信号】 discovered + not at all 否定转折后才是真意 。答案句以 The very first thing that scientists discovered 引出发现，紧跟 was not at all the Earthly paradise that fiction had portrayed 一个强否定，先推翻浪漫想象；随后 nearly identical to our own planet 才正面给出真实结论——否定之后的正面陈述才是科学发现的落点。 

 【替换】 nearly identical to our own planet in bulk properties such as mass, density, and size ↔ resembles Earth in many aspects identical=resembles，逐项列举概括成 many aspects 

 【排除】 B) 与原文相反 原文明明说金星 was not at all the Earthly paradise that fiction had portrayed——根本不像小说写的；It is the same as fiction has portrayed. 偏说 "和小说写的一样"，把原文的强否定 not at all 整个反了过来，是正话反说。  借用原文：Venus was not at all the Earthly paradise that fiction had portrayed 

 C) 与原文相反 原文里 Earthly paradise 是被 "not at all" 否定掉的对象，第 2 段也只说金星 Venus quickly lost its romance（失去了浪漫色彩）；It is a paradise of romance for alien life. 反把这份被否定的浪漫当成发现，与原文相反。  借用原文：not at all the Earthly paradise 

 D) 过度推断 原文后文确提到金星有 a tortured volcanic history（剧烈火山史）和活跃地表，但本题答案句强调的是金星 "在质量、密度、大小上像地球"，并未说它 "像地球一样发生地质变化"；It undergoes geological changes like Earth. 把不同段落的信息硬拼、超出了本题答案句，是过度推断。  借用原文：suggested a tortured volcanic history
questions.spoken_text: What are scientists' findings about Venus?

questions.prompt: What information did Russian and American space probes provide about Venus?
options: It might have been hotter than it is today.
It might have been a cozy habitat for life.
It used to have more water than Earth.
It used to be covered with rainforests.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What information did Russian and American space probes provide about Venus? 

 【翻译】 俄罗斯和美国的太空探测器提供了关于金星的哪些信息? 
 A)  它过去可能比现在更热。 
 B)  它过去可能是生命的宜居栖息地。 
 C)  它过去拥有比地球更多的水。 
 D)  它过去被雨林覆盖。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） It might have been a cozy habitat for life. 
 【定位】 P6 Russian and American spacecraft also found hints that its ancient climate might have been wetter, cooler, and possibly even friendly to life. 
 俄美航天器还发现了线索，表明金星远古时期的气候可能更湿润、更凉爽，甚至可能适合生命存在。 

 【信号】 found hints + ancient climate 是来源与时间的双信号 。Russian and American spacecraft also found hints 直接对上题干来源，its ancient climate might have been wetter, cooler, and possibly even friendly to life 给出关于 "远古气候" 的发现——来源词 + 过去时间词双双命中，正是答案句。 

 【替换】 possibly even friendly to life ↔ a cozy habitat for life friendly to life = cozy habitat for life 
 might have been wetter, cooler ↔ might have been 保留 might have been 的推测口吻 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 原文清清楚楚说远古金星气候 wetter, cooler（更湿更凉），It might have been hotter than it is today. 偏说 "可能比今天更热"，与原文 cooler 完全相反，是把凉听成热的反向陷阱。  借用原文：its ancient climate might have been wetter, cooler 

 C) 偷换概念 原文说金星当初的水 much more water than the tiny trace we find blowing in the thick air today——是 "比今天金星上的痕量水多"，比较对象是金星的现在，不是地球；It used to have more water than Earth. 把比较对象换成 Earth，借 water 这个原词答非所问。  借用原文：much more water than the tiny trace we find blowing in the thick air today 

 D) 未提及 原文讲远古金星是 warm oceans, probably rich with organic molecules, splashing around rocky shores（温暖海洋拍打着岩岸），通篇没提雨林；It used to be covered with rainforests. 凭 "温暖湿润" 自行脑补出 rainforests，属无中生有。
questions.spoken_text: What information did Russian and American space probes provide about Venus?

questions.prompt: What does the speaker mainly study?
options: Causes of sleeplessness.
Cross-cultural communication.
Cultural psychology.
Motivation and positive feelings.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker mainly study? 

 【翻译】 说话者主要研究什么? 
 A)  失眠的原因。 
 B)  跨文化交流。 
 C)  文化心理学。 
 D)  动机和积极情绪。 

 【答案】 C （主旨题） Cultural psychology. 
 【定位】 P1 I specialize in Cultural Psychology, examining similarities and differences between East Asians and North Americans. 
 我专攻文化心理学，研究东亚人与北美人之间的异同。 

 【信号】 开篇自报领域的 specialize in 。I specialize in Cultural Psychology 用 specialize in（专攻于）直接报出研究领域，这种自我介绍式的点题句就是主旨题的答案信号，开头一响就该锁定。 

 【替换】 I specialize in Cultural Psychology ↔ Cultural psychology. 领域名几乎原样对应 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 后文确实大谈 sleep，A 的 Causes of sleeplessness. 借"睡眠"勾人，但讲者研究的是文化如何塑造睡眠，从未把"失眠成因"当作主攻领域，属答非所问。  借用原文：We've also started to look at how culture shapes sleep. 

 B) 偷换概念 Cross-cultural communication. 与原文 Cultural Psychology 都含"cultural"，但把落脚词偷换成 communication（沟通），而讲者明说的是 psychology（心理学），词面相近、内核已变。  借用原文：I specialize in Cultural Psychology 

 D) 答非所问 Motivation and positive feelings. 对应第二段 self-enhancing motivations, how people have positive feelings，那只是文化心理学之下的一个研究分支，被当成"主要研究"就是以偏概全。  借用原文：cultural differences in self-enhancing motivations, how people have positive feelings towards not only themselves
questions.spoken_text: What does the speaker mainly study?

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about North Americans?
options: They attach great importance to sleep.
They often have trouble falling asleep.
They pay more attention to sleep efficiency.
They generally sleep longer than East Asians.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say about North Americans? 

 【翻译】 说话者对北美人有何评价? 
 A)  他们非常重视睡眠。 
 B)  他们经常难以入睡。 
 C)  他们更关注睡眠效率。 
 D)  他们通常比东亚人睡得更久。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） They generally sleep longer than East Asians. 
 【定位】 P3 East Asians on average sleep about an hour and a half less each night than North Americans do. And it's not a more efficient sleep, not like they're compressing relatively more value out of their hours. 
 东亚人平均每晚比北美人少睡约一个半小时。而且这并不是更高效的睡眠，并非他们在更短的时间里压榨出更多的睡眠价值。 

 【信号】 对比结构 less…than 锁定时长差 。East Asians on average sleep about an hour and a half less each night than North Americans do 用 less…than 的横向对比直接给出两群人的睡眠时长关系，这种对比句正是细节题的答案信号。 

 【替换】 East Asians on average sleep about an hour and a half less each night than North Americans do ↔ They generally sleep longer than East Asians. 比较方向对调的同值改写 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 They attach great importance to sleep. 听着合理，但原文只比时长、从未说北美人"重视睡眠"，属未提及。 
 B) 未提及 They often have trouble falling asleep. 讲入睡困难，原文从未提及谁"难入睡"，把不存在的特点安到北美人身上。 
 C) 原词陷阱 原文 And it's not a more efficient sleep 明确否定"东亚人睡得更高效"，C 的 They pay more attention to sleep efficiency. 盗用 efficiency 一词却拼成"北美人重视效率"，既偷换对象又违背原文否定。  借用原文：And it's not a more efficient sleep, not like they're compressing relatively more value out of their hours
questions.spoken_text: What does the speaker say about North Americans?

questions.prompt: How did the speaker conduct the sleep study?
options: By asking people to report their sleep habits.
By observing people's sleep patterns in labs.
By having people wear motion-detecting watches.
By videotaping people's daily sleeping processes.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 How did the speaker conduct the sleep study? 

 【翻译】 说话者如何开展睡眠研究? 
 A)  通过让人们报告他们的睡眠习惯。 
 B)  通过在实验室观察人们的睡眠模式。 
 C)  通过让人们佩戴运动检测手表。 
 D)  通过录像记录人们的日常睡眠过程。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） By having people wear motion-detecting watches. 
 【定位】 P4 Our experiment does not take place in a sleep lab. Instead, we lend people motion-detecting watches, and they wear them for a week at a time. 
 我们的实验并不在睡眠实验室里进行。相反，我们借给受试者动作监测手表，让他们每次连续佩戴一周。 

 【信号】 转折 Instead 后才是真做法 。Our experiment does not take place in a sleep lab. Instead, we lend people motion-detecting watches 先否定"实验室"、再用 Instead 引出真实做法，转折/否定之后的内容才是答案落点。 

 【替换】 we lend people motion-detecting watches, and they wear them ↔ By having people wear motion-detecting watches. 操作描述几乎原样对应 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 By asking people to report their sleep habits. 的"让人自报睡眠习惯"原文从未提及，方法只有戴手表一种，属未提及。 
 B) 与原文相反 By observing people's sleep patterns in labs. 盗用原文 sleep lab 一词，但讲者明说 does not take place in a sleep lab，实验室恰恰是被否定的方式，与原文相反。  借用原文：Our experiment does not take place in a sleep lab. 

 D) 未提及 By videotaping people's daily sleeping processes. 的"录像"原文完全没出现，只是另一种听着合理的监测手段，属未提及。
questions.spoken_text: How did the speaker conduct the sleep study?

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about research on sleep?
options: It has made remarkable progress in the past few decades.
It has not yet explored the cross-cultural aspect of sleep.
It has not yet produced anything conclusive.
It has attached attention all over the world.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say about research on sleep? 

 【翻译】 说话者对睡眠研究有何评价? 
 A)  它在过去几十年取得了显著进展。 
 B)  它尚未探索睡眠的跨文化方面。 
 C)  它尚未产生任何确定性结论。 
 D)  它引起了全世界的关注。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） It has not yet explored the cross-cultural aspect of sleep. 
 【定位】 P6 Sleep is something that has really been an unexplored topic cross-culturally. 
 在跨文化层面上，睡眠一直是一个尚未被探索的课题。 

 【信号】 结尾概括句 unexplored…cross-culturally 。末段 Sleep is something that has really been an unexplored topic cross-culturally 用 unexplored（未被探索）对睡眠研究下了整体判断，篇章结尾的这种概括句是现状题的答案信号。 

 【替换】 an unexplored topic cross-culturally ↔ It has not yet explored the cross-cultural aspect of sleep. 形容词否定转主动否定的同值 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 It has made remarkable progress in the past few decades. 说研究进展大，但原文反复讲 We are still in the exploratory stages 与 an unexplored topic，恰是"刚起步、尚未探索"，与选项相反。  借用原文：We are still in the exploratory stages of this project 

 C) 偷换概念 It has not yet produced anything conclusive. 同样含 not yet，但说的是"没有定论"，原文从未谈"有无结论"，只说"未探索跨文化"，把对象从"探索范围"偷换成"研究结论"。  借用原文：Sleep is something that has really been an unexplored topic cross-culturally.
